chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when he passed over a dry excrement, so he trod upon it, and it hit his garment. So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you have trodden upon an excrement and it hit your garment.' He said, 'Is it not dry?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'There is no problem, for the earth cleanses part of it with part of it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does treading on dry feces make the shoe or ground impure in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *tathir al-ard* (the earth's purifying nature) by ruling that dry feces (*azirah*) does not necessitate washing the shoe or ground upon which it is trodden. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between dry and wet impurities, emphasizing that the earth acts as a natural purifier for dry excrement, thereby simplifying ritual purity for daily movements.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I was with Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> when he<sup>asws</sup> passed upon a dry excrement, so he<sup>asws</sup> trod upon it, and it hit his<sup>asws</sup> cloth. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! You have trod upon a filth and it hit your<sup>asws</sup> clothes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Was it not dry?’ So I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem. Part of the ground (soil) cleans part of it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Once I was in the company of abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and on passing (stepping on) some dried up human feces, certain pieces came in contact with his clothes. I informed him about it and he (the Imam) asked, ‘Was it not dried up?’ I said, ‘Yes, it was dried up.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It (touching) then is not harmful. Certain parts of earth cleanse other parts.’”
